synopsis: Sensor simulation adds a model that must itself be validated; photorealistic appearance alone is insufficient, and camera, lidar, radar and ultrasonic responses require separate simulation layers and material data [f470, f13068, f85, f86]. Across chapters, no validated off-road sensor models or fidelity thresholds were found, standardized quality metrics are lacking, and dust is identified as the biggest gap; evidence for snow, glare and darkness remains weak or absent [f5763, f5764, f5217, f89, f6488]. Lidar is described as the best-validated sensor type, but weather evidence is mostly on-road, and the 2021 lidar dust-cloud model compared with experiments was vendor-coauthored rather than independent evidence of broad off-road qualification [f12604, f7087, f6380]. Planning should start the environment and sensor-model pipeline in October 2026, with calibrated models for one or two sensor types in clear and dusty conditions only conditional mid-2027 targets; production-intent validation depends on sensor selection, mounting and calibration data [f3771, f860, f861]. The recommended use is qualification-quality testing of selected sensor effects and corner cases, feeding detection delay, range and error into braking simulation; compute costs span more than three orders of magnitude, and ten continuously running GPUs over four months provide at most about 29,000 GPU-hours [f4474, f6487, f4451, f8313].
